clue.text: Volume — old book

parts.note: a quart is a measure of liquid volume

explanation.surface: A librarian describes an antique tome by its size.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Volume' looks like the definition, a book, but it supplies the measure QUART.
explanation.definitionFit: A quarto is a book made from sheets folded into four leaves, so it names a kind of book.

clue.text: Who, on the Continent, hang a collaborator?

parts.note: qui is French for who, French being a Continental language
to sling something is to hang it loosely, as a hammock is slung

explanation.surface: A grim question about how Europeans punish those who helped the enemy.
explanation.walkthrough: Vidkun Quisling led Norway's puppet government under the Nazis, and his name became a byword for a traitor.
explanation.definitionFit: Eponym: the Norwegian wartime puppet leader's surname became a common noun for a traitor who works with occupiers.

clue.text: Bill gets sheep to misbehave

parts.note: AC is short for account, which is a bill
a tup is a ram, a male sheep

explanation.surface: A farmer called Bill finds his flock unruly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' reads as a man's name but gives AC, an account.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to act up is to behave badly or play up, as children do.

clue.text: Draw Asian into discussion

indicators.note: put into discussion, the word is spoken, so its sound counts rather than its spelling

parts.note: a Thai is a person from Thailand, in Asia

explanation.surface: Someone tries to involve an Asian colleague in a debate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Draw' looks like a verb meaning attract, but it is the noun for a level result.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a match ending level is a draw or a tie.

clue.text: Pond is initially wet, specially when temperature has dropped enough

indicators.note: specially, as in arranged in a special way, tells us to rework these letters
initially picks out only the opening letter of the word is

explanation.surface: A naturalist notes that a pond turns damp as the air cools.
explanation.walkthrough: 'specially' rearranges POND, I (the first letter of 'is') and WET.
explanation.definitionFit: The dew point is the temperature at which air, cooling, becomes saturated and dew forms.

clue.text: Make capital out of achievement

definitions.meaning: to profit or take advantage from something

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb meaning take advantage of and a noun meaning a daring feat.

clue.text: Beatrix's hero safe, with teacher on time

parts.note: peter is old criminal slang for a safe
a rabbi is a Jewish religious teacher

explanation.surface: A children's author's protagonist arrives punctually with a schoolteacher.
explanation.walkthrough: PETER for a safe is safecracking slang (a peterman blows safes).
explanation.definitionFit: Beatrix Potter's most famous character is the mischievous young rabbit in the blue jacket.

clue.text: Very rude about that bankrupt

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for rude goes round the abbreviation

parts.note: insolent means rude or impertinent

explanation.surface: A creditor complains about the impoliteness of a bankrupt debtor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts INSOLENT round V; 'that' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone insolvent cannot pay debts, which is to be bankrupt.

clue.text: Rhyme describing gigolo

parts.note: a rhyming two-part term for a young man kept by an older lover

explanation.definitionFit: Slang: a young man who is the lover of an older woman, the two halves rhyming exactly.

clue.text: Gloomy policeman with nothing to eat

indicators.note: to eat is to take in, so the policeman's name holds the zero

parts.note: Inspector Morse is the famous fictional Oxford detective
O, the figure zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: A hungry police officer is understandably sullen.
explanation.walkthrough: MORSE is the Oxford detective of novels and a long-running British TV series.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone morose is sullen and gloomy.

clue.text: Noodles may be having problems

definitions.meaning: literally where noodles are served, in a bowl of broth
the idiom for being in trouble

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means in difficulty, and noodles are literally found in a bowl of broth.

clue.text: Soldiers given filthy accommodation will be appealing

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve soldiers
a sty is a pigpen, proverbially filthy housing

explanation.surface: Troops offered squalid barracks might still find them attractive.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something tasty, especially food, is appealing or delicious.

clue.text: Hal, up on roof, dancing in celebration of victory

indicators.note: dancing letters move about, so these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone called Hal dances on a rooftop to mark a win.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dancing' rearranges HAL, UP, ON and ROOF; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: winners take a circuit of the arena to receive the crowd's applause.

clue.text: Without any preparation, because of money

parts.note: from can mean owing to, as in tired from work
scratch is slang for money

explanation.surface: Someone acts on impulse, motivated by cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to start from the very beginning, with nothing prepared beforehand.

clue.text: Contribution to whole of sign

indicators.note: a contribution is a part given, so only a run of letters is taken from these words

explanation.surface: A remark that something adds to the meaning of a symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the Lion is one of the twelve signs of the zodiac.

clue.text: Offensive number is nothing to me

parts.note: O, the figure zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: Someone shrugs off an insulting figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: noisome means unpleasant or offensive, especially of smells.

clue.text: Athlete, in training, takes rice

indicators.note: training changes a body's shape, so these letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: A sportsperson eats rice as part of their training diet.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: someone who skates competitively on ice is a kind of athlete.

clue.text: He's managed to find ammunition

definitions.meaning: one who has tracked something down
a bullet leaving a visible trail

explanation.definitionFit: The word is one who traces things and also a bullet that leaves a visible trail.

clue.text: Are Derby disposed to loaf?

indicators.note: disposed means set out in order, so the letters are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: A question about whether a football team is inclined to laze around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loaf' looks like a verb, idling, but it is the noun for bread.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: rye bread is commonly baked as a loaf.

clue.text: What's thrown out of planes approaching America?

indicators.note: approaching means coming up to, so the planes come right before America

parts.note: jets are aircraft

explanation.surface: Someone asks what gets dumped from aircraft nearing the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: Jetsam is goods jettisoned from a ship, thrown overboard to lighten it.

clue.text: I landed in the end, after raising levy

indicators.note: in places these letters inside the other piece
raising lifts the word upward in this down clue, so it is written backwards

parts.note: an aim is an end or goal
lit means landed, as a bird lit on the branch

explanation.surface: A parachutist reports finally touching down after a tax was raised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after raising' reads upward in this down clue, giving MIA; 'levy' is the noun for troops called up, not a tax.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a levy is a body of troops raised for service, as a militia is.

clue.text: Two shillings added to river boat's rope

parts.note: a bob was a pre-decimal British shilling, so two of them are bobs
the Tay is a Scottish river

explanation.surface: A small sum is spent on a rope for a river boat.
explanation.walkthrough: The shilling was a pre-1971 British coin, nicknamed a bob.
explanation.definitionFit: A bobstay is a rope or chain holding a ship's bowsprit down to the stem.

clue.text: Somewhat tanned member of youth organisation, we hear

indicators.note: we hear tells us the word is spoken, not spelt

parts.note: a Brownie is a junior Girl Guide

explanation.surface: A young scout has picked up a light suntan.
explanation.definitionFit: The suffix -y means somewhat, so the word describes a colour tending towards brown.

clue.text: Forced to leave lop

definitions.meaning: to cut off a branch with a saw

explanation.definitionFit: Past tense, it means drove someone away; as a verb, it means cut a limb off by sawing.

clue.text: Island loses second vessel

indicators.note: loses means a letter is dropped from the island's name

parts.note: Sark is one of the Channel Islands

explanation.surface: An island community is deprived of a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Noah's ark is the most famous vessel of that name.

clue.text: Practical approach apparent when Tom was in charge

definitions.meaning: a rough method based on experience
the reign of the tiny folk hero Tom Thumb, read whimsically

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means a practical rough guide, and read literally it is the reign of Tom Thumb.

clue.text: Open up, letting in racist who's lost key

indicators.note: letting in means one word takes another inside it
who's lost means the racist's word drops a letter

parts.note: a Nazi is a fascist, held to racist ideology
A is a musical key

explanation.surface: A door is unlocked by a bigot who mislaid his key.
explanation.walkthrough: 'who's lost' drops A from NAZI to leave NZI.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to unzip a bag or jacket is to open it.

clue.text: Players retired to set about other things

indicators.note: retired means withdrawn or gone back, so the result is read backwards
set about means placed around, so one word encloses the other

parts.note: etc. means and other things

explanation.surface: Retired sportsmen busy themselves with other pursuits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set about' makes TETCO; 'retired' turns it round. 'Players' suggests sportsmen, but here it means musicians.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a group of eight musicians playing together is an octet.

clue.text: Old car, one with Dutch IVR, endlessly dithers about

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the cut word goes around the others
endlessly means the final letter is cut off

parts.note: tizzies are states of nervous dithering
I is the Roman numeral one
NL is the international vehicle registration code for the Netherlands

explanation.surface: An old motor with Dutch plates wobbles about uncertainly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' leaves TIZZIE. IVR codes are the country letters on cars driven abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Tin Lizzie was the nickname of the Ford Model T, a cheap early car.

clue.text: One about to show resentment

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Someone is about to express their annoyance.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: ire is anger, close to resentment.

clue.text: Deaf hero's wrinkled brow

indicators.note: wrinkled means creased out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A hard-of-hearing champion frowns with a furrowed brow.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the brow is the forehead, the part of the face above the eyes.

clue.text: Fully laden, man took off

parts.note: he is the male pronoun, standing for a man
to take someone off is to mimic them, to ape

explanation.surface: A heavily loaded man sets off on a journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'took off' suggests departing but means imitated.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a heaped plate or cart is piled full.
